subject: general
question: Due to which of the following HIV infection does not occur in humans?

options.text: Sharing syringes when injecting drugs intravenously
In a child born to an HIV-positive mother

solution:
The correct answer is __**HIV infection cannot be transmitted by sharing toilets with an HIV-positive person.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus)** is a virus that attacks the **immune system** of the human body, making it difficult for the body to fight **infections and diseases.**
 
• HIV can be transmitted through the **exchange **of certain **bodily fluids, including blood, semen, vaginal fluids, and breast milk.**
 
• However, HIV** cannot be transmitted** through casual contact such as sharing toilets, utensils, or hugging.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Repeated blood transfusions** can actually increase the risk of HIV transmission if the donated blood is **not screened properly** for the virus.
 
• **Sharing needles or syringes** while taking medications can also increase the risk of HIV transmission as the virus can be present in the blood of an infected person.
 
• **HIV-positive mothers **can transmit the virus to their babies during** pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding**.
 
• However, with **proper medical care **and treatment, the risk of mother-to-child transmission can be significantly reduced.
 
• It is important to note that HIV infection is preventable through safe** sex practices, avoiding sharing needles or syringes, and getting tested **regularly for the virus.
 
• **Treatment options **are also available to manage the virus and prevent it from progressing to AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome).
